sections.label: Public consultation on draft Bill
sections.summary: A public consultation on the draft Bill ran from 4 May to 25 May, and MOF evaluated feedback and incorporated it where relevant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: A public consultation exercise on the draft Bill was held from 4 May to 25 May this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) has evaluated the feedback received and, where relevant, incorporated them in the final Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: First, amendments relating to the Valuation Review Board; second, amendments to clarify and enhance information gathering for tax compliance purposes; and third, amendments relating to digital property tax notices.

sections.label: Digital notices consent or opt-out
sections.summary: The Act will be amended so digital notices can be sent to taxpayers who consented or who did not opt out after being notified.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: To enable more taxpayers to benefit from digital channels, the Act will be amended so that digital notices can be sent to taxpayers who have either consented to receiving digital notices, or who have not opted out after having been given notice that they will be issued with digital notices.

sections.label: Digital notices on opt-out basis
sections.summary: Digital notices are on an opt-out basis, so people must specifically choose paper notices, and the speaker presumes IRAS will send hardcopy notices to everyone.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One of these is the use of digital notices by taxpayers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is on an opt-out basis, meaning people will have to specifically choose to receive paper notices.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I presume the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) will send hardcopy notices to everyone, telling them what is about to happen.

sections.label: Confirming notice preferences with users
sections.summary: The speaker says penalising her would be grossly unfair and hopes IRAS will contact users, maybe older ones, to confirm their notice preference.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If we then penalise her for it, it will be grossly unfair.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope IRAS will contact users, maybe those above a certain age who have not used digital notices before, to confirm with them whether they want digital or paper notices.

sections.label: Elderly may overlook one letter
sections.summary: The speaker says a single letter or an English-only letter might be overlooked, and hopes IRAS confirms with the elderly before switching them to digital notices.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If IRAS only sends out one letter, or the letter is only in English, some Singaporeans might overlook it.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that when dealing with the elderly, IRAS can confirm with them first before changing the notification into digital notices.

sections.label: Bill refines appeals and digitises communications
sections.summary: The amendment Bill seeks to refine the appeals process, protect the tax base by strengthening enforcement and information gathering, and digitise IRAS-taxpayer communications.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If we want to move towards a Smart Nation, can the Government step up efforts to protect Singaporeans' online safety?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This amendment Bill seeks to refine the appeals process and protect our tax base by strengthening enforcement and information gathering powers and digitising the communications between IRAS and our taxpayers.

sections.label: IRAS stronger enforcement powers
sections.summary: The Bill amends the law to give IRAS stronger enforcement powers, including new section 64A granting full and free access to premises, documents and computers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill makes bold amendments to provide IRAS with stronger enforcement powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I refer particularly to the new section 64A which gives IRAS “full and free access to all houses, buildings, lands, documents, computers, computer programmes and computer software”.

sections.label: Increased fines and imprisonment
sections.summary: The maximum fine rises from $2,000 to $10,000 and imprisonment from three to 12 months, benchmarked against the GST Act, and the Member asks if case numbers explain the increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The increase from the current maximum fine of $2,000 to $10,000, and an imprisonment term from a maximum of three months to 12 months, is a significant jump.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that this increased figure is benchmarked against the GST Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I do support the increase in penalties to act as deterrence, but can the Minister clarify if these increases are due to an increase in cases of hindering and obstructing?

sections.label: Phased implementation of digital notices
sections.summary: IRAS intends a phased approach, starting with Property Tax notices for individuals, then Property Tax notices for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As Mr Henry Kwek suggested, what IRAS would do is that it intends to adopt a phased approach to its implementation and start with Property Tax notices for individuals first, then followed by Property Tax notices for businesses.

sections.label: Digital platform taxpayers notified
sections.summary: Starting with taxpayers already on the digital platform, covering over 55% of residential properties, hardcopy letters in October 2017 will notify them of digital tax notices from 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, what this means is that we will start with people who are already transacting with IRAS on the digital platform.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Such residential properties make up over 55% of residential properties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In October 2017, these taxpayers will receive hardcopy letters notifying them of IRAS' plans to issue digital tax notices for property tax payable from 2018.

sections.label: Excluded flats and elderly owners
sections.summary: IRAS will exclude one- and two-room HDB flats and individual residential property owners aged 70 and above this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In addition, IRAS will exclude one- and two-room Housing and Development Board flats and individual residential property owners who are aged 70 and above this year.

sections.label: Notices not sent to personal email
sections.summary: The digital tax notices and the notice for payment will not be sent to the taxpayer's personal email account.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As explained earlier, the digital tax notices and the notice for payment will not be sent to the taxpayer's personal email account.

sections.label: Property Tax information gathering powers
sections.summary: The amendment enhances Property Tax Act information gathering powers and aligns them with the Income Tax, GST and Stamp Duty Acts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The amendment will enhance the information gathering powers under the Property Tax Act, align the information gathering powers under the Property Tax Act with existing information gathering powers under the Income Tax Act, GST Act and Stamp Duty Act.

sections.label: Machinery property tax exemption feedback
sections.summary: The machinery property tax exemption amendment was not included in the Bill as feedback is still being studied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the proposed amendment on exemption of machinery from property tax.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This was not included in the Bill as we are still studying the feedback and we will, in due course, make a decision on the feedback received.
